The Six Continents.text: The world is known to contain six continents surrounding the Lake Mobius interior: the Republic of Padokea (a constitutional democracy in East Gorteau region), Yorknew (an island nation analogous to the United States), NGL (a Luddite narco-state on the western coast), East Gorteau (a former puppet dictatorship), the Kakin Empire (an absolute hereditary monarchy recently admitted to international recognition), and Meteor City (a scavenger settlement of the stateless). The geography of the world is vast and perilous, with mountain ranges, jungles, and vast deserts separating regions. Most international travel occurs by sea, rail, or contracted airship. The interior of the Lake Mobius is officially unmapped and off-limits—the V5 nations maintain a territorial consensus that nothing lies beyond the outer coastlines worth investigating.

The Republic of Padokea.text: Padokea is a constitutional republic in the eastern part of the known world, best known as the homeland of the Zoldyck family. The nation is mountainous and rural in its interior, with the city of Kukuroo as a major pilgrimage and tourism draw—the Zoldyck Testing Gate is publicly accessible, though no visitor has ever passed its gates. Padokea's government is stable but lightly centralized, with local lords holding considerable autonomy. The Zoldyck family is the nation's most famous export: world-class assassins whose legend reaches every corner of the globe. The nation's economy relies heavily on mercenary contracts, mining, and tourism related to the Zoldyck mystique.

Yorknew City and the Island Nations.text: Yorknew is the largest and most cosmopolitan city in the known world, located on an island nation that serves as the global center of commerce, finance, and underground trade. The city is known for its underground auction houses where anything can be bought: artwork, nen-infused artifacts, rare animals, and relics of historical value. Yorknew is the headquarters of the Ten Dons—the mafia overlords who control organized crime globally. The city is heavily policed on the surface but lawless below ground; the Mafia families operate with impunity, and the Ten Dons command absolute loyalty from their subordinate families. The nation has a constitutional monarchy, but the Ten Dons hold true power.

NGL and the Western Coast.text: NGL is a small, isolationist nation on the western coast known for its Luddite philosophy—rejecting technology, electricity, and external cultural influence. The nation is ruled by a warlord named Gyro and is a major producer of illegal narcotics exported to neighboring regions. NGL's borders are heavily fortified, and the nation actively kills outsiders who cross into its territory. The interior is densely jungled and home to numerous magical beasts of unusual size and ferocity. Hunters rarely venture into NGL, and fewer return; the nation's interior is virtually unmapped.

East Gorteau.text: East Gorteau is a politically volatile region in the eastern part of the known world. For centuries it was governed as a loose confederation of city-states until recently falling under the control of a puppet dictator installed by foreign powers. The region is known for its extreme wealth disparity, baroque culture, and history of civil strife. The current government is nominally democratic but widely understood to be a puppet regime. East Gorteau is strategically vital for international trade routes and access to the interior regions. The military is strong but poorly motivated; many soldiers are conscripted rather than volunteer.

Kakin Empire.text: The Kakin Empire is a vast, hereditary autocracy ruled by the immortal dictator Nasubi Hui Guo Rou. It is the largest nation by land mass and population, stretching across multiple climate zones and dominated by a rigid caste system. The empire was long considered too remote and inhospitable for international engagement, but recent diplomatic overtures have led to its admission to the V5 council of nations. Kakin's military is massive and well-disciplined; its navy is second only to Yorknew's merchant fleet. The nation is home to numerous martial traditions and nen-using warrior castes who serve the imperial family. The succession question—how power passes when Nasubi dies—is a closely guarded state secret, though rumors of internal strife among his children suggest the matter is far from settled.

Meteor City.text: Meteor City is a scavenger settlement built in the ruins of an ancient meteor impact, home to the stateless poor and outcasts of the known world. The city has no formal government; survival is based on scrounging, theft, and barter. Most citizens were born in Meteor City or were abandoned there as children. Officially, the city barely exists in the eyes of the major nations—it is off the maps, unrecognized, a place of urban legend and danger. In truth, Meteor City has a hidden power structure and organizational hierarchy that rivals organized crime syndicates. The city has produced some of the world's most dangerous individuals.

The Hunter Association.text: The Hunter Association is an independent, quasi-governmental organization that licenses Hunters—individuals granted near-total legal immunity in exchange for maintaining professional standards and completing commissioned work. The Association has approximately 600 licensed Hunters worldwide, with ranks from rookie to double-star. The headquarters is a fortress of bureaucracy and training facilities located in an undisclosed location accessible only to licensed members. The Association's chairman is its absolute authority; the current chairman is Isaac Netero, a living legend who is said to be the strongest Nen user alive. The annual Hunter Exam is held under the Association's auspices; it is brutally selective, with thousands of applicants and only a handful passing. Examinees are often forced to kill, betray, or destroy one another to pass. The Hunter license grants its bearer legal immunity for actions taken in pursuit of licensed contracts, making Hunters de facto above the law.

The Hunter Exam.text: The Hunter Exam is conducted annually by the Hunter Association to identify and select individuals of exceptional ability and character. The exam is held in secret locations and rotates between different regions each year. Examinees are drawn from all walks of life; age is no barrier, and children as young as ten compete alongside adults. The exam consists of multiple phases testing physical endurance, problem-solving, and often combat. The pass rate is intentionally brutal—fewer than one percent of applicants ever become licensed Hunters. Examiners are themselves famous Hunters, each bringing their own philosophy and moral flexibility to the examination. The exam is known to kill candidates; deaths are rule-breaking on the examiners' part but not unheard of. Those who pass become members of the Hunter Association and receive a hunter license granting them near-total legal immunity.

Hunter License Tiers and the Star System.text: Hunter licenses are ranked by the number of stars a Hunter earns over their career. A rookie Hunter has no stars and limited authority; a one-star Hunter has proven significant accomplishment and can undertake more dangerous commissions; a double-star (two-star) Hunter is a veteran with major achievements and high status; a triple-star Hunter is exceedingly rare and commands respect globally. Star rank is awarded by the Hunter Association based on completed contracts, discovered knowledge, and demonstrated skill. The star system creates a power hierarchy within the Association; higher-star Hunters receive better contracts, higher pay, and first claim on research opportunities. The current strongest living Hunter, Isaac Netero, is a legendary figure of indeterminate star rank—older than the current star system itself.

The Phantom Troupe.text: The Phantom Troupe is a band of elite thieves and assassins, thirteen strong, known for coordinated heists of extraordinary scale and brutality. The Troupe is infamous for stealing priceless artifacts, murdering entire families, and leaving no witnesses. They are identifiable by distinctive spider tattoos bearing numbers from 0 to 12 on their bodies. The Troupe's internal structure is mysterious; their leader is known only as Chrollo Lucilfer (#0), and the identity and abilities of most members are unknown to law enforcement. The Troupe emerged roughly five years before the present era and has committed some of the most heinous crimes in recorded history, yet law enforcement remains unable to apprehend them. They are considered the most dangerous criminal organization in the world, more feared than the mafia syndicates themselves.

The Scarlet Eyes Massacre.text: Roughly five years before the current era, the Kurta clan—a reclusive, peaceful tribe known for their unique scarlet-colored eyes—was systematically slaughtered. The massacre was perpetrated by the Phantom Troupe, who harvested the victims' scarlet eyes for sale on the black market. Scarlet Eyes are highly prized by collectors and are rumored to enhance certain Nen abilities, commanding astronomical prices at underground auctions. The massacre became public knowledge: the Kurta clan was destroyed, the Scarlet Eyes circulate widely among wealthy collectors and criminals, and the perpetrators remain unidentified and at large. The massacre is remembered as one of the cruelest acts in recent history.

The Mafia Community and the Ten Dons.text: Organized crime is structured globally around the Ten Dons—ten crime lords who rule their respective territories absolutely. Below the Ten Dons are hundreds of mafia families, each operating with strict hierarchy and codes of loyalty. The Ten Dons coordinate on major decisions affecting global crime; they meet rarely and in absolute secrecy. The Mafia controls most underground commerce: smuggling, illegal trades, assassination contracts, and the black market for stolen goods. The Mafia has its own code of honor; betrayal is punished by death, and internal disputes are settled through direct violence. Mafia families often hire Hunters as mercenaries or bodyguards, creating an overlap between legitimate and criminal power. The Ten Dons themselves are rarely seen in public; their identities and faces are closely guarded secrets known only to upper-level family members.

Heavens Arena.text: Heavens Arena is a massive, 251-floor combat tower located in a major city, where fighters from across the world compete in one-on-one matches for prize money and prestige. Fighters are ranked by the floor they can reach; higher floors hold stronger competitors. The prize pool is enormous; a single championship can net a fighter millions. Heavens Arena is also a cultural institution where the wealthiest patrons gather to gamble, socialize, and witness exceptional combat talent. The lower floors are chaos—novices, cheaters, and sandbagging veterans preying on newcomers. Higher floors are home to legitimate elite fighters with international reputations. Floor 200 marks a significant threshold: above it, combat becomes truly lethal, and the strongest independent fighters hold court. The Arena employs rules and referees but is ultimately a brutal meritocracy where the strong dominate the weak.

The Zoldyck Family.text: The Zoldyck family is the world's most renowned assassination family, living in fortress seclusion on Kukuroo Mountain in the Republic of Padokea. The family is led by patriarch Silva and his wife Kikyo, with children including the eldest son Illumi, the second son Milluki, and the youngest Killua. The Zoldycks are famous for their absolute skill in killing—no Zoldyck contract is ever left unfulfilled, and their success rate is perfect. The Testing Gate at the base of Kukuroo Mountain is legendary: the gate's weight increases dramatically with each of its five doors, and no outsider has ever passed through. The Zoldyck family is also famous for their brutal internal training regime; children are raised as assassins from infancy. The family is wealthy beyond measure and maintains connections to every criminal organization globally. They are employed by the world's most powerful people and most dangerous criminals alike. The family is patriarchal and absolute in its hierarchy.

Magical Beasts.text: The world is home to numerous species of magical beasts—creatures whose bodies and abilities defy ordinary nature. Magical beasts range from small, human-sized predators to enormous monsters capable of destroying cities. Some species are rare and confined to specific regions; others are common enough to be hunted for their bodies, which can be sold for valuable materials. Beast biology is poorly understood by mainstream science; most research is conducted by Hunters specializing in zoology. Some beasts possess natural Nen-like abilities—the capacity to manipulate their own bodies or the environment around them in ways that seem magical. Beasts can be domesticated, though this is rare and dangerous; the Zoldyck family employs a massive guard hound named Mike. Many beasts are carnivorous and actively hunt humans; regions known to contain particularly dangerous beasts are avoided by common travelers.

The V5 Nations.text: The V5 is an international council of the five most powerful nations in the known world: the Republic of Padokea, Yorknew, NGL, East Gorteau, and the Kakin Empire. The V5 meets in secret to coordinate policy on matters of global importance, including international trade, military affairs, and the control of sensitive information. The V5 is known only to the highest echelons of government and to the Hunter Association's leadership; the general public is unaware it exists. The V5 maintains a strict consensus on territorial boundaries and strategic interests, making open war between member nations unthinkable. The V5 also coordinates on the most sensitive topics: the location and nature of restricted zones, the control of information about the world's true geography, and the suppression of research into certain historical mysteries. Recent intelligence suggests the Kakin Empire has recently been admitted to the V5, restructuring it as the V6, though this has not been publicly acknowledged.

Nen as Hidden Discipline.text: Nen is a hidden discipline taught to a select few who demonstrate exceptional ability and mental fortitude. To the general public, Nen is rumor and legend—stories of 'trained auras' and mysterious powers possessed by certain Hunters and martial artists, nothing more. The Hunter Association controls Nen knowledge carefully; Nen users undergo a formal 'baptism' where their aura nodes are forcibly or gently opened, allowing them to perceive and manipulate aura. Once awakened, a Nen user sees the world differently—aura becomes visible to their eyes, and they can sense the presence and intentions of other Nen users. Nen is taught in stages, with foundational techniques like Ten (aura control), Zetsu (aura suppression), Ren (aura amplification), and Hatsu (personal ability) forming the core curriculum. The discipline requires decades of dedicated practice to master. Nen knowledge is heavily restricted; teaching Nen to an untrained person is considered reckless, as Nen awakening without proper mental preparation can cause psychological breakdown or death.

Ten, Zetsu, Ren, and Hatsu.text: Nen's foundational techniques are Ten, Zetsu, Ren, and Hatsu. Ten is the baseline state for a trained Nen user—the constant circulation and control of aura through the body, preventing aura leakage and maintaining defensive capability. A master of Ten can maintain it indefinitely without fatigue. Zetsu is the inverse: the deliberate suppression of all aura, rendering the user invisible to Nen perception and abandoning all Nen defense. Zetsu is used for stealth and escape, but leaves the user defenseless against Nen-based attacks. Ren is the amplification and projection of aura outward, increasing physical power, speed, and durability while broadcasting one's presence to all nearby Nen users. Ren is the aggressive state, used in combat and intimidation. Hatsu is the development of a personal Nen ability unique to each individual, often reflecting their personality, values, or fighting style. Hatsu can range from simple techniques to extraordinarily complex powers, and mastery of Hatsu is the mark of a true Nen adept.

The Six Categories and Water Divination.text: Nen users are classified into one of six natural categories, determined by how their aura manifests and behaves. The six categories are Enhancement (aura that amplifies the user's physical body), Transmutation (aura that changes properties and characteristics), Conjuration (aura that creates solid objects from nothing), Emission (aura that is projected away from the body), Manipulation (aura that controls external objects or other beings), and Specialization (aura that violates normal Nen rules in unique ways). A Nen user's category is discovered through Water Divination: the user holds a glass of pure water, concentrates their aura, and observes what happens. If the water overflows, the user is an Enhancer; if it changes taste, they are a Transmuter; if impurities appear, a Conjurer; if a leaf moves, a Manipulator; if the color changes, an Emitter; if something else entirely occurs, a Specialist. Most Nen users are strongest in their native category and weaker in adjacent or opposite categories. The hexagon of affinities shows that each category is adjacent to two others and opposite to one other. Specialization occupies a unique position, adjacent to Conjuration and Manipulation.

Hexagon Affinity and Category Efficiency.text: The six Nen categories form a hexagon of relative affinity: Enhancers are adjacent to Transmuters and Emitters, two steps away from Conjurers and Manipulators, and opposite to Specialists. Each user is most efficient (100% output) in their native category, efficient (80%) in adjacent categories, moderately efficient (60%) two steps away, and least efficient (40% or less) in opposite and non-adjacent categories. A user can learn techniques outside their category, but doing so requires more aura, more training, and yields weaker results. For example, an Enhancer attempting Conjuration (two steps away) will succeed at 60% efficiency, meaning their conjured objects are weaker or less stable than a Conjurer's would be. Specialists occupy the center of the hexagon and have unique affinities; they are strongest in Specialization itself and adjacent to Conjuration and Manipulation. The hexagon system reflects a deep truth about Nen: your natural talent aligns with your fundamental nature, and working against that nature carries a steep cost.

Vows and Limitations.text: A Nen user can bind themselves with a Nen vow—a formal, binding commitment to a specific condition or limitation. In exchange for this binding, the user's Nen power increases dramatically. For example, a Nen user might vow to fight only a single opponent for the rest of their life, gaining massive power increases against that opponent in exchange for weakness against all others. Vows are absolute; breaking a vow results in the user losing all the power granted by that vow and suffering severe aura backlash or, in extreme cases, death. Vows are not magical contracts—they are psychological bonds that reshape the user's aura structure itself, reflecting their commitment. The stronger the vow and the more absolute the limitation, the greater the power gain. Vows can be temporary (binding for a specified time) or permanent (binding until death). A user can harbor multiple vows simultaneously, but each additional vow adds complexity and risk. Vows are personal and unique; no two users' vows are identical.

The Aura Baptism and Forced Awakening.text: The process by which a Nen user first awakens their aura is called the baptism. A Nen instructor forcibly or gently opens the candidate's aura nodes, flooding their body with Nen for the first time. The experience is excruciating; the sensation is described as burning from within, as if the body is being remade. Most candidates who undergo baptism without proper psychological preparation suffer severe trauma or death. Those who survive emerge transformed: they can now sense aura, maintain Ten indefinitely, and begin the long process of learning Nen techniques. The baptism is irreversible; once a user is awakened, they remain Nen-capable for life. The trauma of baptism shapes how a Nen user views the discipline; many awakened users speak of it as the moment they truly became aware of the depth of human potential. Instructors like Wing of Heavens Arena serve as guides through this threshold.

Nen After Death and Grudge.text: When a Nen user dies, their aura does not simply dissipate—it can linger in the world as Grudge Nen, especially if the user died under conditions of intense emotion, injustice, or unfinished purpose. Grudge Nen is hostile and chaotic; it seeks to inflict suffering on the living. The strongest Grudge Nen manifests as literal ghosts that can interact with the physical world, growing more dangerous and unpredictable as time passes. Haunted locations can be identified by the presence of Grudge Nen; exorcising a haunted place requires a powerful Nen user to either convince the Grudge to pass on or forcibly disperse it. Some Nen users attempt to bind their consciousness into their Grudge Nen before death, preserving a shadow of themselves beyond death. These attempts are rarely successful, but when they are, the result is a near-immortal entity of pure malice. The existence of Grudge Nen is known to Nen users but is kept secret from the general public, as it would cause widespread panic if people knew that the dead could linger as hostile entities.

ARC 1: The Hunter Exam Era.text: [ARC: Hunter Exam — Year 0] The 287th Hunter Exam is underway, with thousands of applicants competing for the honor of becoming licensed Hunters. The exam is notorious for its brutality; examinees are often forced to kill one another to progress. The current examiners are Satotz (Phase One), Menchi (Phase Two), Buhara (Phase Two), and Lippo (Phase Three, the tournament bracket). Among the examinees are several who will become notable figures: Gon, a young boy from a remote island seeking his father; Kurapika, the sole survivor of a recent tragedy; Leorio, a young man seeking wealth and medical knowledge; Killua, an escaped assassin; and Hisoka, a dangerous psychopath who failed the exam the previous year. The world does not know of Nen's existence; rumors of 'trained auras' circulate among Hunters, but the general public is ignorant. The Phantom Troupe's identities remain unknown, and the Kurta massacre is remembered as a historical tragedy with perpetrators unidentified. Isaac Netero is alive and serves as the Hunter Association's chairman, though his true power remains his personal secret. Greed Island has not yet been discovered. SECRET: Nen exists and is being taught to those who pass the exam. The Zoldyck family's youngest member, Killua, is competing under a false identity. Gittarackur is actually Illumi, Killua's oldest brother, sent to ensure Killua fails the exam. Hisoka's category and personal ability remain unknown.

ARC 2: The Zoldyck Estate.text: [ARC: Zoldyck Family — Year 0, weeks after exam] Killua has been retrieved from the Hunter Exam by his family and returned to Kukuroo Mountain. His companions—Gon, Kurapika, and Leorio—have journeyed to the Testing Gate to retrieve him, facing the gate's escalating weight challenges and the family's defensive retainers. The Zoldyck family is revealed as a dynasty of assassins led by Silva and Kikyo, with children trained from infancy for killing. The family's internal dynamics are cold and utilitarian; love exists, but it is expressed through trials and tests. Illumi, the eldest, acts as the family's agent in the outside world. Killua has begun to question his family's values after meeting Gon, sparking internal conflict. The family's Nen techniques remain largely hidden from outsiders. SECRET: Alluka exists but is sealed away on the estate, a secret even from most Zoldyck staff. Illumi has placed a needle in Killua's brain during childhood, allowing him to control Killua's actions; this needle remains undiscovered. Silva harbors a distant history with Chrollo Lucilfer, leader of the Phantom Troupe, though the nature of their relationship is unknown.

ARC 3: The Heavens Arena Training.text: [ARC: Heavens Arena — Year 0-1] Gon, Kurapika, and Killua have entered the 251-floor Heavens Arena to train and compete for prize money. Wing, a legitimate Nen instructor and guardian of the arena's upper floors, agrees to teach the three the fundamentals of Nen. This marks their first true training in Nen; they learn Ten (aura control), Zetsu (aura suppression), Ren (aura projection), and begin Water Divination to determine their Nen category. The arena's lower floors are chaotic and filled with dangerous fighters who prey on newcomers. Floor 200 marks the threshold where Nen training becomes mandatory; above it, combat becomes genuinely lethal. Hisoka appears in the arena as a floor master, observing talent and occasionally fighting. His Nen ability, Bungee Gum, is revealed as a Transmutation technique with properties of both rubber and gum. SECRET: The Phantom Troupe's membership is still hidden; Hisoka's spider tattoo is discovered to be fake, and he is not truly a member of the Troupe. Kastro, a mirror-double specialist, faces Hisoka and is defeated. Ging is only a name whispered on a tape recording Gon discovered.

ARC 4: The Yorknew Auction and Phantom T.text: [ARC: Phantom Troupe & Yorknew — Year 1, September] The world's most prestigious underground auction is underway in Yorknew City, with artifacts, stolen goods, and treasures from across the globe on display. The Nostrade family, led by patriarch Light Nostrade, is in attendance with his daughter Neon, whose Nen ability, Lovely Ghostwriter, allows her to make accurate prophecies—though the family keeps this secret. Kurapika has been hired as a bodyguard and has awakened his Nen as a Specialist, forming a Scarlet Eyes vow that grants him superhuman power against spider members. The Phantom Troupe has chosen this auction as their hunting ground, planning a massacre to steal the merchandise. The troupe's roster includes Chrollo (#0), Nobunaga (#1), Feitan (#2), Machi (#3), Phinks (#5), Shalnark (#6), Franklin (#7), Shizuku (#8), Pakunoda (#9), Bonolenov (#10), Uvogin (#11), and Kortopi (#12); Hisoka (#4) is an imposter, and Kalluto later joins. The Ten Dons of the mafia are present, making the event both glamorous and treacherous. Uvogin confronts Kurapika and dies, marking the first major casualty. The Phantom Troupe fakes their deaths via Kortopi's Nen ability. Chrollo's Nen is sealed by Kurapika's Judgment Chain, preventing him from using Nen or contacting his members. Hisoka abandons the Troupe. Gon discovers a tape recording from Ging about the existence of Greed Island. SECRET: Greed Island is not a video game but a Nen-constructed island created by Ging and ten masters. Meteor City is the Phantom Troupe's true homeland, a connection known only within the Troupe. Kurapika's vow is absolute: he can kill any spider member without hesitation or moral consequence, but his eyes turn completely black and his lifespan shortens with each use.

ARC 5: Greed Island.text: [ARC: Greed Island — Year 1-2] Greed Island is discovered to be a real island created entirely through Nen, not a video game. The island exists in the physical world and can be entered by those who obtain a copy of the game or are brought by another player. Ging, Gon's father and the island's creator, is revealed as a legendary double-star Ruins Hunter who created Greed Island with the help of game masters including Razor (an extremely powerful Nen user), Eta, Elena, and others. The game operates on a card-based spell economy; players collect cards from monsters and other players to complete the game's objectives. Biscuit Krueger, who has been posing as a young boy named Bisky, is revealed to be a 57-year-old double-star Hunter with a hidden muscular true form. She becomes the group's trainer, pushing Gon and Killua through brutal Ren training that expands their aura capacity and forces them to master advanced Nen techniques. The Bomber trio (Genthru, Sub, and Bara) terrorizes players, forcing them to surrender hard-earned cards via a Countdown Nen ability that kills if the timer expires. The climax involves a dodgeball game against Razor and his companions, where Hisoka's Bungee Gum is used in combat. At the game's end, 'Accompany' card transports Gon to meet Kite. SECRET: Kite is a legendary Hunter and Ging's apprentice, a single-star who is more powerful than he appears. The Chimera Ant threat does not yet exist; the game's final card is not understood to be a prophecy of coming darkness.

ARC 6: The Chimera Ant Catastrophe.text: [ARC: Chimera Ant — Year 2-3] A Chimera Queen, a parasitic monster capable of consuming other creatures and birthing hybrid offspring, washes ashore in NGL—a narco-state ruled by the warlord Gyro. The Queen begins reproducing, creating hundreds of humanoid soldier ants with human intelligence and Nen abilities. The ants spread across the nation, consuming the population and establishing a new society. Kite, leading an expedition to study the ants, is killed by one of the Queen's strongest offspring, the Royal Guard Neferpitou. Gon and Killua arrive too late to save him, triggering a spiral of despair. The Queen continues her breeding cycle and eventually gives birth to Meruem, the Chimera Ant King—a being of superhuman intellect and power who immediately kills his mother and assumes control of the ant civilization. Three Royal Guards are born: Neferpitou (the Doctor, whose Terpsichora allows time manipulation), Shaiapouf (the Manipulator, whose Beelzebub allows pheromone control), and Menthuthuyoupi (the Emitter, whose powers involve rage and weaponized aura). Meruem relocates to East Gorteau, a puppet dictatorship he plans to rule directly. The Hunter Association mounts an invasion force including Isaac Netero himself, Zeno (Zoldyck elder), and Morel. Netero confronts Meruem and detonates a Nen-bomb containing Poor Man's Rose, poisoning the King and dying in the explosion. Meruem, though poisoned, defeats the invasion and eventually dies with Komugi, a human girl who befriended him, at his side. Gon, broken by Kite's death, makes a desperate vow and is transformed into an adult version of himself in exchange for all his Nen, allowing him one catastrophic strike against Neferpitou before collapsing into a coma. SECRET: Kite is not dead but reborn as a Chimera Ant—a red-haired humanoid ant child, though her memory of her past life is absent. Gon is Nen-less after his transformation; his recovery is not guaranteed. Rose (Poor Man's Rose) was a Nen bomb created in secret by Netero decades before, and its existence was a closely guarded state secret. The Zodiacs (the 12-member elite council of the Hunter Association) exist but operate in shadow; most of their existence and identities remain unknown.

ARC 7: The 13th Chairman Election.text: [ARC: 13th Chairman Election — Year 3] Isaac Netero is dead, killed in the Chimera Ant invasion. The Hunter Association must elect a new chairman through a complex voting procedure. Pariston Hill (a mysterious Zodiac member ranked as Rat) serves as the Association's vice-chairman and orchestrates a series of games designed to test the candidates. The Zodiacs—twelve elite Hunters holding zodiac code names—are revealed to the public for the first time. Pariston (Rat), Mizaistom (Ox), Kanzai (Tiger), Pyon (Rabbit), Botobai (Dragon), Gel (Snake), Saccho (Horse), Ginta (Sheep), Saiyu (Monkey), Cluck (Chicken), Cheadle (Dog), and Ging (Boar) represent the Association's inner sanctum. Ging is revealed to be Gon's father, a legendary Ruins Hunter and Zodiac member of indeterminate star rank. Gon remains comatose in the Association's medical care. Killua, now a full Nen user, learns of his sister Alluka's existence and her Nen ability: wish-granting at escalating prices. Alluka heals Gon, restoring his physical health but leaving him Nen-less as a permanent consequence of his vow. Illumi, working with Hisoka (who has been hunting Troupe members), attempts to recapture Killua and Alluka, but Killua's needle is removed, unlocking his latent ability Godspeed. Pariston wins the election but immediately resigns, allowing Cheadle Ddf (Dog) to become the 14th chairman. Gon meets Ging at the World Tree, though their relationship remains unresolved. SECRET: Alluka is not human but a Gas-Life form from the Dark Continent, discovered and brought to the Zoldyck family by Silva. Nanika, the wish-granting entity within Alluka's body, is Alluka's true nature; the two entities are distinct but inseparable. Saiyu, a Zodiac member, is secretly working as a mole for the Kakin Empire. The Dark Continent's existence and the V5's suppression of knowledge about it is revealed only at the arc's end, via Beyond Netero's announcement of an expedition.

ARC 8: The Dark Continent Expedition and.text: [ARC: Dark Continent Expedition & Succession War — Year 3-4, ongoing] Beyond Netero (Isaac Netero's son, long presumed dead) announces his intention to mount a full expedition to the Dark Continent—a forbidden region beyond the known world that the V5 has kept secret for generations. The V5 is expanded to V6 by admitting the Kakin Empire, a massive autocracy under the immortal Nasubi Hui Guo Rou. The Kakin Empire dispatches a royal vessel, the Black Whale, carrying 200,000 passengers, including 14 princes competing in a succession war for the imperial throne. Each prince is bonded to a Nen beast—a parasitic guardian entity born from the prince's own vow and desires—that protects them but also kills rivals in the succession. Kurapika, now operating as a Zodiac member (Rat, after Pariston's departure), serves as bodyguard to Woble (prince 14) and her mother, Queen Oito. Tserriednich (prince 4) is revealed as an extraordinarily dangerous Nen prodigy and serial murderer with a Specialist ability granting future-sight; he collects Scarlet Eyes as trophies. The Phantom Troupe has boarded the Whale, hunting Hisoka in retaliation for his murders of Kortopi and Shalnark. Hisoka, having died and self-revived through his Nen ability, is aboard seeking vengeance and bodies to fight. The Five Calamities of the Dark Continent are referenced but not fully revealed: Brion, Zobae, Hellbell, Ai, and Pap—mysterious entities of extreme danger that have prevented exploration. Ai is a Gas-Life form theoretically connected to Nanika, hinting at the Dark Continent's biological strangeness. The Zodiacs are aboard the Whale, with Mizaistom guarding Beyond and the mole Saiyu orchestrating betrayals. The voyage is ongoing, and the continent's interior remains unmapped and unknown. EXTRAPOLATED — BEYOND PUBLISHED MANGA: The ultimate outcomes of the Succession War, encounters with the Five Calamities, and Beyond's true intentions for the continent remain unresolved in the published manga (through chapter 410). All events beyond this point are speculative. The story continues, but its conclusion is yet unwritten.

Five Calamities of the Dark Continent.text: The Dark Continent is home to five entities classified as Calamities—threats of existential magnitude that have prevented human colonization and exploration. These are Brion, Zobae, Hellbell, Ai, and Pap. Brion is theorized to be a massive parasitic organism capable of consuming entire ecosystems. Zobae is described as a disease vector of extreme lethality. Hellbell is believed to be a chimeric predator of incalculable power. Ai is a Gas-Life form—a sentient, amoeba-like entity of unknown intelligence and hunger. Pap is classified as an unknown threat whose nature is not yet understood. The Five Calamities have been contained or deterred by the Kakin Empire's historical blockade of the continent, a military effort that has cost thousands of lives. The threat they pose is so severe that the V5 (now V6) maintains absolute secrecy regarding the continent's existence to prevent panic. Beyond Netero's expedition is explicitly forbidden by international law, and his mere announcement triggers geopolitical crises.

Lake Mobius and the Interior.text: Lake Mobius is the massive, interior body of water surrounding which the six known continents have developed. The interior of the lake is officially unexplored and unmapped. The V5 maintains a consensus that the lake contains the Dark Continent—a forbidden zone that is off-limits to all exploration and colonization. This consensus is maintained through economic pressure, military threat, and information suppression; no official world map acknowledges the Dark Continent's existence. The lake is ringed by dangerous whirlpools, deep-water predators, and mysterious phenomena that make conventional navigation nearly impossible. Ancient charts from pre-V5 eras hint at lands beyond the lake's interior, but these are dismissed as myth or legend by mainstream scholarship. In truth, the Dark Continent exists; the V5 has chosen to keep it secret from the world's population to prevent resource conflicts, territorial wars, and inevitable human casualties from attempting to settle the continent. The interior of the lake is the world's greatest secret.

Beyond Netero and the Expedition.text: Beyond Netero was the son of Isaac Netero, the legendary Hunter Association chairman, and was presumed dead decades ago. Beyond has recently resurfaced with an explicit goal: mounting a full-scale expedition to the Dark Continent in defiance of international law and the V5's consensus. Beyond is a triple-star Ruins Hunter and a legitimate scholar of ancient history, giving his claims credibility despite their legal and political impossibility. His expedition has attracted media attention, curiosity-seeking Hunters, and the attention of major nations. The expedition's true goal remains unclear—scientific discovery, resource extraction, or something darker. Beyond's legitimacy as a Hunter and scholar makes his expedition a genuine threat to the V5's information control. His announcement has triggered a cascade of events, including the expansion of the V5 to include the Kakin Empire and the mobilization of the Hunter Association's highest-level members. Beyond's fate and the true nature of his intentions remain unresolved.

The Kakin Empire's Rise.text: The Kakin Empire, long isolated from international affairs, has recently emerged as a major global power through careful diplomacy. The empire is ruled by Nasubi Hui Guo Rou, an immortal dictator whose methods of achieving immortality are unknown. Nasubi has multiple children (at least 14 princes and likely more), and the question of succession has long been his personal obsession. The empire's military is vast and disciplined, rivaling or exceeding the military forces of the other V5 nations. Kakin's admission to the V5 (now V6) represents a geopolitical shift; the empire has leverage over the other nations and is suspected of harboring territorial ambitions. Kakin's interior practices extreme martial discipline and Nen training, with warrior castes serving the imperial family. The empire is known for its complex court intrigue, where princes scheme against one another and alliances shift constantly. Kakin's culture is foreign and often disturbing to outsiders; practices that would be illegal elsewhere are normalized within the empire. The succession question is the empire's greatest source of instability and power; whichever prince claims the throne will reshape the empire and the global balance of power.

The Hunter Association's Zodiac Council.text: The Zodiacs are twelve elite Hunters holding the highest rank and authority within the Hunter Association. Each Zodiac is given a zodiac code name (Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Sheep, Monkey, Chicken, Dog, Boar) and serves as an advisor to the Chairman or the Association's leadership. The Zodiacs are among the most powerful Nen users in the world; their exact abilities and identities are closely guarded. The Zodiacs' influence extends beyond the Association into global politics; many nations consult with Zodiacs on matters of state security. The Zodiacs maintain contact with one another through secure networks and meet in secret to coordinate major decisions. The existence and identities of most Zodiacs remain unknown to the general public; even among Hunters, Zodiac membership is a closely held secret. The Zodiac council is headed by the Chairman, who serves as the ultimate authority over the Association's policies and operations. The Zodiacs wield power proportional to their rank, star rating, and political connections; some are more influential than others.

Greed Island and the Game Masters.text: Greed Island is a Nen-constructed island created by Ging Freecss and ten game masters—elite Nen users who collaborated on the island's design and function. The game operates on a spell-card economy; players collect cards by defeating monsters, trading with other players, or completing specific challenges. The game has multiple objectives, the ultimate goal being to reach the final card, 'Accompany,' which transports the player to meet the game's creator. Ging created Greed Island as a time capsule and a test—a way to leave a message for Gon while also filtering for individuals of exceptional talent and determination. The game masters include Razor, a legendary Nen user of the Emission category, and others whose identities remain unknown to the game's players. Greed Island exists in the physical world and is protected by barriers that prevent uncontrolled entry or exit. The island's internal rules are enforced by Nen itself; objects and rules created within the game cannot be violated by physical force alone. Greed Island is a monument to Ging's genius and his attempt to control the circumstances of his reunion with Gon.

The Scarlet Eyes Black Market.text: Since the Kurta massacre five years ago, Scarlet Eyes have circulated on the black market as luxury items for collectors and combatants. The eyes are highly prized for their aesthetic beauty and rumored enhancement properties; some Nen users claim that possessing a pair grants perceptual or combat advantages, though these claims are unverified. The price for a single pair has reached astronomical figures—millions of units of currency. The eyes are most sought after by wealthy collectors, criminal organizations, and Nen specialists who believe they carry latent power. The underground auction houses of Yorknew feature Scarlet Eyes as premium auction lots, attracting bidders from across the globe. The black market trade in Scarlet Eyes has spawned a subculture of eye traders, thieves, and assassins who specialize in acquisition and sales. The eyes are identifiable by their distinctive crimson color and the small, pupil-like marking in the iris. Very few complete pairs remain intact, making individual eyes even more valuable.

Water Divination: The Methodology.text: Water Divination is the canonical method for determining a Nen user's natural category. The process is performed by a trained Nen instructor and requires the student to have recently undergone baptism (aura node opening). The student is given a glass of pure water and instructed to concentrate their aura while the instructor observes. The water responds to the student's aura in one of six ways, revealing their category: Enhancers cause the water to overflow; Transmuters change its taste; Conjurers introduce impurities; Manipulators move a floating leaf; Emitters change its color; Specialists cause something entirely different to occur. The methodology is not fully understood by most Nen users; it appears to reflect something fundamental about how each category's aura interacts with inert matter. Wing, the Heavens Arena instructor, teaches Water Divination as part of basic Nen education. The test is reliable and repeatable; a student tested multiple times will receive the same result. Water Divination is considered the most accurate method for identifying a student's natural Nen category.

Hunter Association.text: The Hunter Association is an independent, quasi-governmental organization that licenses Hunters—individuals granted near-total legal immunity in exchange for maintaining professional standards and completing commissioned work. They manage the annual Hunter Exam, maintain the star-rank system, and enforce licensing standards across approximately 600 active Hunters worldwide. The Association is respected by governments and feared by criminals as the world's most powerful neutral force.

Phantom Troupe.text: The Phantom Troupe is a legendary phantom band of elite thieves, assassins, and killers numbering exactly thirteen members, identifiable by distinctive spider tattoos bearing numbers from 0 to 12. They coordinate heists and murders of extraordinary scale and brutality, stealing priceless artifacts and leaving no witnesses to their crimes. Law enforcement globally fears them as the most dangerous criminal organization in the world, yet the identities and faces of most members remain unknown to the public.

Zoldyck Family.text: The Zoldyck family is the world's most famous and feared assassination dynasty, residing in fortress seclusion on Kukuroo Mountain in the Republic of Padokea. They maintain a perfect contract fulfillment record; no Zoldyck contract is ever left uncompleted, and no witness survives. Their Testing Gate is legendary: the gate's weight increases across five doors, and no outsider has ever passed through, making the family's seclusion absolute.

Mafia Community.text: The Mafia Community is the world's organized crime structure, ruled by the Ten Dons—ten crime lords who exercise absolute authority over their respective territories and hundreds of subordinate families. They control all major underground commerce including smuggling, assassination contracts, black-market trades, and illegal trafficking. The Ten Dons coordinate on global decisions but rarely meet in person, maintaining a code of honor where betrayal is punished by death.

Chimera Ant Colony.text: The Chimera Ant Colony is a rapidly evolving hive organism led by a sentient Queen capable of consuming other creatures and integrating their genetic material into her offspring. The colony produces humanoid soldiers of escalating intelligence and power, from mindless drones to elite Royal Guards possessing impossible Nen abilities. The colony exists in complete secrecy—the public has never learned of their existence.

Kakin Royal Court.text: The Kakin Empire is a vast, hereditary autocracy ruled by the immortal dictator Nasubi Hui Guo Rou, stretching across multiple climate zones with a rigid caste system and massive military. Recently admitted to international recognition as a sixth great power, Kakin commands a navy second only to Yorknew's merchant fleet and is home to numerous martial traditions and Nen-using warrior castes. The empire is a rising third-world power rapidly transitioning to great-power status through military and diplomatic pressure.

The Zodiacs.text: The Zodiacs are twelve senior Hunters serving as Chairman Netero's inner council, each bearing a zodiac animal codename that reflects their personality or role within the Association. They function as the Association's highest authority beneath the Chairman and maintain direct access to classified information, deep lore, and strategic decision-making. The Zodiacs are the living embodiment of the Association's true power, far more influential than any star-ranked Hunter.

Nostrade Family.text: The Nostrade family is a mid-tier mafia clan that has risen suspiciously fast to prominence in Yorknew's underground auction circuit within the past decade. The family maintains a veneer of legitimacy as wealthy patrons and collectors, while secretly operating one of the world's most profitable criminal enterprises. Their sudden ascent from obscurity to power suggests hidden resources or extraordinary talent.

East Gorteau Regime.text: East Gorteau is a politically volatile region governed as a puppet dictatorship under the figurehead Ming Jol-ik, with a nominally democratic constitution that masks absolute authoritarian control. The regime maintains a facade of legitimacy while suppressing dissent through military force, and the region is strategically vital for international trade routes. The military is strong but poorly motivated, composed largely of conscripts rather than volunteers.

Greed Island Game Masters.text: The Greed Island Game Masters are the anonymous creators and administrators of Greed Island, the world's most expensive and exclusive game, said to be playable only by those who possess both the game cartridge and access to specialized technology. The masters are themselves a faction of elite Nen users who maintain the game's day-to-day operations, enforce rules, and control the card economy. The game's existence is known only to the wealthiest collectors and those willing to pay millions to play.

Meteor City Community.text: Meteor City is a scavenger settlement built in the ruins of an ancient meteor impact crater, home to the stateless poor, orphans, and outcasts of the known world who have no official existence on any nation's maps. The city has no formal government; survival is based on scrounging, theft, barter, and the unwritten law that outsiders who touch its people face absolute retaliation. Most citizens were born in Meteor City or were abandoned there as infants.

Battera's Clear Campaign.text: Battera's Clear Campaign is a standing bounty established by the wealthy billionaire Battera, offering enormous financial reward to anyone who can clear the Greed Island game—entering the game, finding the Book, completing the card collection, and achieving victory. The campaign attracts elite Hunters and ambitious players willing to risk millions in the hope of claiming Battera's prize. Battera himself operates in shadow, hiring intermediaries to manage contracts and recruitment.

Black Whale Expedition.text: The Black Whale Expedition is humanity's first officially sanctioned voyage to the Dark Continent under the leadership of Beyond Netero (Chairman Netero's estranged son), carrying approximately 200,000 passengers including Hunters, scholars, adventurers, and political representatives from the V6 nations. The expedition represents an unprecedented challenge to the global consensus that the Dark Continent is unexplorable and uncharted, and marks a pivotal moment in world history. The voyage occurs aboard the Black Whale, a massive ship capable of supporting a floating city.

V5 (The Five Great Powers).text: The V5 is a supranational council comprising the five great powers of the known world—the Republic of Padokea, Yorknew, NGL, East Gorteau, and Kakin—that coordinates on matters of mutual interest including trade, military alliances, and the regulation of the Dark Continent. The council maintains a facade of democratic cooperation while each nation pursues its own strategic interests. The V5's primary function is to enforce a global consensus: the Dark Continent is unexplorable and the world map officially shows six continents surrounding Lake Mobius.
